Still, if a company is unable to provide the smaller car we requested --and would have preferred-- they should still honor the price.  Cars provided should be in better repair.  My next car rental in Europe will use a different agency.  It is also worth noting that nobody was at the place in Sorrento where we were supposed to pick up the car until about a half-hour after we were scheduled. The 24 hour helpline is a message bank that says to call back during office hours and the number provided to call would not connect.: We paid up front for our car. We got off the flight collected our luggage and walked out into the very small area of the Rome airport which is open at night. A few men were standing with placards just through the doors where everyone walking through from the flight could see them. We could not help but see them and their placards but none had our names on them and we hadn't expected them to as our instructions told us to ring the number provided. I immediately tried to ring the number provided and it did not connect. I tried a few times and then walked over to the information desk and asked the guy to try for me. He did. He tried on my mobile, on the information desk phone line and on his personal mobile. He said this number does not connect, what is the company name I will google them. I gave him the paperwork and he tried the 24 hour helpline. It went straight to a message bank that said to call back between Monday and Friday, during the hours 9-5. He tried a few times. He said I am sorry there is nothing more that I can do. If you wait over there, I will keep trying. We stood near the drivers with their placards and waited. He kept trying both the numbers in between helping other people. We waited until midnight and my daughter was sobbing her heart out. She thought the whole trip was ruined and a lot of the accommodation she had booked was non refundable and she thought we had lost that money and the money from the car hire. We were so tired and so afraid and had no idea what to do. The information guy came over and said you are going to have to get a cab to your accommodation or a bus. He had written down the bus line to catch and the cost of a cab to our accommodation. Pay no more than this amount for the cab, he said firmly. He was so kind and helpful. We walked out the front and the buses had stopped running it was so late so we forked out 55 euros for a cab to our hotel. We arrived and our hostess kindly took the car paperwork and said she would try and sort the car out for us in the morning while we caught up on some sleep. I emailed DriveAway immediately, telling them what had happened. We got up the next morning and our hostess had had no luck connecting to the number provided or to the 24 hour helpline. It was still going to the answering machine. We suspect the number provided to call was not replaced on the receiver as we called it without problem after we had the car and during office hours. Whether his was intentional or not I don't know. We had a walk around the city but it was hard to relax not knowing if our money was completely lost or if we would even be having the driving holiday we planned. We received an email from DriveAway saying they were sorry that had happened and provided an email to contact the Rome office on. Better than nothing I suppose. We heard nothing more and we got up the next morning and had to book another hotel to check into as we had to check out of ours as they were full. We had booked a place in orbotello that we were supposed to be driving to. We paid for another cab to the next hotel. We were an extra 300 euro out of pocket between the cabs and the extra nights accommodation in Rome. I emailed DriveAway and told them I expected to be reimbursed for all my expenses that were a result of not having the car I had paid for as well as the days of hire that I had paid for but did not have the car. DriveAway did not reply to this. I was supposed to get the car Friday night but only heard from the car company on Sunday afternoon, after I had had to check into the next hotel. I said it would have to be Monday that I pick the car up then. I received no apology just an excuse that his boss had been there with a placard, which was simply not true either. We got the car in the end but no compensation for all the extra expenses or a refund for the days without the car that I had paid to have it. Useless company and rude as well. Never again for me.

But the absence of local stores with home theater seating in stock made it necessary to go the online route.  The Home Meridian seats are just as the sales person described, and the white glove installation was a pleasant experience. If you are considering these seats, be aware that the backs are high, which is what I wanted and makes them quite comfortable for big and small bodies.  However, if your theater has multiple rows of seats and is not elevated at least 2 steps per level, the view of the screen can be blocked when the seats in front are in the full upright position.  These seats are quite wide as well, providing a great experience as long as you have the room width and don't need more seats in each row, which may be possible with a smaller style seat.  Also worth noting is that each chair has 2 power cords as the LED's lighting for the control and cup holders is on it's own supply cord, so you will most likely need power strips to accommodate the many cords.  It seems like a simple design change would allow a single cord per chair as well as daisy chaining the row into a single cord, but this is only a minor inconvenience.  The only thing I would seriously like to see on these seats, other than a massage option, is the ability to dim or disable the blue LED lights on the controls, as they are distracting in a dark theater. I would be quite comfortable purchasing additional Home Meridian seats from this company and recommending them to others.

The Product and Company are not ready for the US market.: I ordered two of the Kubix Thermostatic Triple Shower with Ceiling Mounted Head and Hand Shower packages, for about $1,150. This is False, every connection (all 12) requires a BSP to NPT adapter, the additional space needed for the BSP adapter is not included in any schematic or diagram so the valve did not fit the intended location.  The adapters do not accommodate a sweat connection and therefore require another threaded adapter to make the connection.  This series of adapters and threaded connections is a leak waiting to happen. The valve and handheld are plumed for 1/2" fittings while the ceiling mount is 3/4" fittings and the package did not include the proper adapter requiring another adapter to connect to the system. The handheld wall outlet elbow is plastic and not brass (side note this is what was damaged in shipping).  Besides being plastic the elbow did not include a backnut to hold it in place on the wall and the threads on the wall side are not long enough to accommodate the provided adapter without buying additional extensions and fittings. With 2 trips to the hardware and an order from another company to replace the wall outlet elbows, I need to  purchase approx $150 of additional adapters and fittings to accommodate the installation of this package. Mediocre security and poor customer service: While I was away for several days my World of Warcraft account was hacked. I used a "strong" password and given that I'm stringent about security upon my own system and email, it became apparent that blizzard doesn't do anything to disallow repeated password failures from "strange" IP address locations. For instance, for the past several years of being a customer I have indeed changed my password often and to complex or difficult passwords. In addition to that I have never logged in outside of my home state or ISP. One would think then that after they sent me a free "Authenticator" at my SAME home address that has ALWAYS been registered to my account since the first day I signed up, that the act of then registering the same serial number of that keychain to my account after it's delivery would suffice as identifying me as still in control of the account. Anyway without offering the ability to bind logins to an ip or region there's very little point in even realisticly having a password, In addition the authenticators are actually very weak if a victim did suffer a keylogger. Once you captured enough authenticator transactions you could likely deduce the base key used to generate the number string used as input. Then if you studied the autheticator itself it could be reverse-engineered into an authenticator "Enigma Machine". I should also state that as long as it was done long enough and discreet enough currently a malicious hacker could just cycle ip addresses and hammer random passwords and eventually grab many accounts regardless of how well protected they are. I should also state that there is software out there that can easily defeat almost, if not ALL "captcha" text systems. To make a point, when you generate a key with the authenticator app/keychain the number generated isn't the only number that will be valid because the keychain has no way to communicate/reset/randomize the variable that actually controls the numbers generated because that very variable is derived from a non-randomized "Key". I do NOT endorse malicious activity to any degree and also DO NOT condone such activities and state these things so that the less informed customer may become better informed about how easily an account can be lost. I never bought gold or anything else from anybody, never broke a rule, and always changed my password. Also during the days,weeks,months that some automated program tried to chip away at my password from a foreign country, you mean to tell me nobody noticed the massive failed attempts that must have occured? Be aware and be safe and my suggestion is that if this happens to you do NOT turn over all of your personal and or private data to Blizzard, as the two methods they allow you to provide them with private data(photo Id,etc.) are through fax and phone. Both of which aren't assured to be secure to any degree. Either way they did me a favor which is why I don't give them a 1, at least after leaving wow and blizzard behind I at least have time to enjoy making music.

As I proceeded through the intersection I heard a load pop and my van came to a grinding halt half way through the intersection.  I pushed through the intersection and pulled over.  My entire right side was sitting on my wheel.  The bolt that is screwed on to the top of the ball joint had popped off.  Who knows how long the cotter pin was the only thing keeping the bolt on.  I found the bolt and the treads were completely stripped and worn.  To fix it I ran to O'Reilly and purchased a new ball joint.  I lifted the van and lifted the arm so the ball joint pushed through steering knuckle.  I took the bolt from the new ball joint and screwed it onto the ball joint I purchased from PartsGeek.  This tells me that the bolt was faulty.  The treads on the ball joint were good enough to take another bolt so I could get the van home, but the bolt was stripped completely bare with worn to were shinny metal was showing.  Had I been going freeway speed I probably would have rolled my van and been seriously injured.  I would like to see PartGeek contact me and ship me a replacement part as soon as possible.  I'm still counting my blessings and thanking the good Lord I was not driving to Park City like I'm supposed to do tomorrow or to Logan like I'm supposed to do on Monday.  I could have died.

For the price of the stone and the price of the ring everybody will also look online for comparison before buying ( i did and i didn t find better), but the most important aspect for me was the relation i had with the stuff at Baunat. As i bought an engagement ring I will remember everything around the it, the moment i decided to buy it, the  moment i bought it, the moment i first had it in my hand and what followed  (that is a private story). In all this, the people who made it for me played a very important part and i took the time to write this in order to thank them, they really deserve it. So , in conclusion, I hope it is the only engagement ring i have to buy in my life(we all hope this), but for sure, for other jewelry items i ll contact Baunat again. PS: I see the ring as a piece of art and the attention to details is fascinating.

I ordered prescription sports sunglasses, but what I received was a regular, nice pair of sports sunglasses, with a small set of frameless prescription lenses that connects to the interior of the nose bridge or piece that rests on the nose. The prescription lenses and the sun shield portion of the sunglasses can separate easily, which makes for a lot of surfaces that need to be kept clean. If these were used for sports, it would be difficult to keep the surfaces clean from sweat, smudges, and debris. To clean well, you must remove the prescription lenses (bare lenses connected by a small but sturdy piece of clear plastic over the nose) from the sun shield, and then you have to clean the inside and outside of the prescription lenses followed by cleaning the inside and outside surfaces of the sun shield. Doing this while standing or sitting without a place to rest one piece while cleaning the other can be difficult to do without smudging the surfaces you just cleaned with fresh fingerprints, or dropping the piece you just cleaned, while trying to clean the other piece. Separating the sun shield from the prescription lenses does have its benefits, but I would like to have known the pieces were separate when browsing or ordering the sunglasses. Separating the two does allow you to change the sun shield with various tints, like amber, clear, or darker/lighter tints. It would also be nice to be able to order additional sun shields and additional prescription lenses separately. I would like to have understood the dual-lense configuration when ordering, since I could have added a darker tint to the prescription lenses, which would have suited my situation nicely (probably uncommon). I was in a car accident that left me with a strong sensitivity to sunlight or even brighter interior lighting. I would love a pair of wraparound sunglasses that can accept prescription lenses inserts, and which allows a variety of darker tinted lenses. I would like a lighter tint when watching TV at night, and the darkest tent possible (while still seeing) for when I need to venture outside, and perhaps even a medium tint for use inside during the day. I would also like to have a good pair of very dark wraparound sunglasses with the prescription lenses integrated into the sun shield. Since I wear sunglasses ALL the time, it would be nice to have this pair for use as my primary pair of glasses, but with only one set of lenses to keep clean. Right now, I use these glasses with the prescription lenses inserts, which I find more challenging to clean and to keep clean. Now, if I could find someone who could make a nice pair of prescription Active Shutter 3D glasses for my 3D LED/LCD TV. If these mythical glasses were rechargeable, then I would pay as much as $200 for a single pair. Actually, I would pay that even if they weren't rechargeable. I am stuck in bed from a car accident, and nothing takes my mind off the pain as well as a good, immersive 3D movie. All in all, my experience was excellent, and I would definitely recommend GlobalEyeglasses to friends and family.

No "Guarding" involved: Identity Guard's name is a case study of marketing hype that doesn't come close to anything in reality.  If named for what Identity Guard actually does, and how well they do it, they should more aptly go by "Alert after the horse has left the barn... often, long after".  One could argue that it's better than nothing, but I would say, not by much.  When my wife's purse was stolen, we called I.D. Guard and were told what we already knew... that we'd have to contact the banks and other organizations to cancel all her cards immediately.  "Duh, really?!"  They couldn't even provide the service of being a one-stop shop, holding the list of all your financial institutions with all your accounts, #'s, and each institutions' lost/stolen hotline numbers.  All your stuff's just been stolen, you don't remember or know all that; you're lucky if you even remember which cards you had in there.  Apparently, the only thing I.D. Guard is capable of doing in that situation is to put some kind of "heightened" level of monitoring on your cards, etc. (leaving one to believe that they're only half-heartedly monitoring them otherwise); and then to notify you after the fact if somebody with your name is opening new accounts, etc.  So as a preventative, there's nothing they do to "guard" your identity from being stolen, they simply sound the alert after it's too late.  That's it. Nada. Nothing else. Even then, often times, any effectiveness at that lower level of service is lost when they take forever to make you aware.  Example, I decided to try out a fee offer of Experian's monitoring service, and signed up for it on 1/13/14.  I wasn't notified by Identity Guard until 3 weeks later of that activity. That doesn't sound to me as though they're guarding ANYthing. However, to be fair, I don't know if any organization has such powers of pre-emptive protection. But then Identity Guard (again, starting with the name itself) shouldn't be saying and/or insinuating in their marketing hype that they can.  And I suppose that if you're in a situation where nothing has been stolen, and there's no reason to believe that someone else is pretending to be you, opening accounts, etc., this service is better than nothing. They notify you of such activity... fine. Even then, I.D. Guard might argue that they do so just as quickly as Experian notifies them (or whomever the reporting organization/bank/etc. is). But again, that's a very far cry from actually guarding it, (i.e.,  protecting it, preventing it from happing, etc.). Therefore, I rate the value of the services they provide vs. what they charge as being poor. I currently pay $18/mo. for the most basic service (and no, nothing above that level provides anything that approaches i.d. theft prevention either).  I'd say it's worth more like $5/mo.

Disappointed - Experience not nearly as good as it could have been: I was excited when I found a replacement radiator for my Nissan Titan on PartGeek for a reasonable price.  It was the part I needed, at a price that I was willing to pay.  As a "do-it-yourself" kind of guy this was going to be a good way for me to save a few dollars over taking it to the repair shop for work.  I read the reviews online, and it seemed that PartsGeek had an excellent reputation. The part arrived, obviously damaged in shipping.  Parts of the radiator were broken off and protruding from the package.  Now, I realize that this criticism should be directed at the shipping company, FedEx, and it has been.  The driver left the package at my house despite it having obvious damage to both the packaging and the contents.  I quick call to FedEx to reject the shipment and they were on their way to pick it back up and return it to PartsGeek. So, I go to the website and send a message letting them know that I've rejected the package and get an autoresponse saying that they will get back to me in 24-48 hours.  This is the only method of communication with PartsGeek, and it's slow.  The responses typically take closer to 48 hours than 24. Beyond that the return and refund experience isn't all that fantastic.  I asked if they could expedite a new part to me so that I could complete my repair.  Then answer is "no" - parts are returned to the warehouse they ship from and they don't do exchanges, they only credit your account back.  If you want another part you have to buy another part, have it shipped and they will refund the first part.  How long does the credit take?  15-30 days according to their message back to me.  This is the most disappointing aspect of the whole experience.  PartsGeek exists and serves a purpose, but in the end they are "drop ship" operation that doesn't appear to own the inventory they sell.  The parts are cheap, and the service you get is exactly what you pay for.  I'm pretty sure they wouldn't accept terms from me that state they should ship me a part, and after I install it and test it for 15-30 days I'll pay them, yet those are the terms of their refund to me.  In the end I'm out the cost of the radiator, I'm out of time and the truck is at the shop getting repaired by my local guy who is going to stand behind his work and do everything he can to make it right. Suggestions for PartsGeek - 1) Take customer service a bit more seriously.  People are buying parts from you because something they have is broken and they want it fixed. Choose your stars accordingly then begin bidding.  Once you have come to an agreed price, purchase room for the single night. The trick is to see where you are booked and if you want to stay at that particular hotel for the entire duration of your stay. If you like the location, Priceline will give you an option in your emailed confirmation to ADD EXTENDED NIGHTS FOR THE SAME PRICE! This way, if you aren't happy with what you got the first time, you can try to do it again and shoot for a better place. You may have to bump up your price $5-10 per night, but in most cases it's worth it. I started my bidding at $35 for a 3 star and ended up at $50 for 3 nights in a really nice Hampton Inn and Suites in a very safe part of town. Just know that the key to compromise is going to be you get what you pay for, even when negotiating...in other words, if you bid at a 2 star price you can't expect to get a 5 star hotel...you still have to be realistic.

The effective date of March 1st, was somehow accelerated to February 1st, and now I owed Humana a lump sum of three times the premium. Both initially claiming it wasn't within their ability to change the enrollment process with their specific company.  Humana told me it was eHeath's responsibility, and eHealth stating they were just the "broker" and had nothing to do with the premiums charged and effective date controversy; this is the "ugly".  I will never get those 7 hours back in my life, but the importance of having health insurance was too great to let things go.  I am still working with Humana in an attempt to "fix" this, and I have hopes that with the evidence I have from eHealth initiation documents that I will get this fixed.  I am disappointed and dissatisfied with the lack of attention I've gotten from eHealth.  They should assist me with getting this straightened out with Humana, but alas, they've washed their hands, stating "We're only the broker."  I'd love to still have their assistance with this, but I'm not willing to spend hours on the phone to do so...We'll see.   But, if I had the opportunity to recommend an insurance broker with you, a friend, it would not be eHealth...I finally was lucky enough to speak to a customer representative, [name], from Humana who assisted me with authoring a grievance to correct the anomaly with the effective date.  However, I did have to pay a two month premium sum in order to remain enrolled in healthcare, not knowing if I'll be charged for the month I really didn't have coverage.  If charged for February, I plan on suing eHealth for this false charge and mental anguish, in small claims court...not because of anything but their lack of willingness to help when they should be....we are not just numbers, we're people with needs.

A good machine let down by a minor build fault and below-par support: System delivered as specified although the packaging between the outer and inner boxes was not great. Could not get sound working from the from front headphone socket. Followed the instructions in the manual but the configuration panel that ought to have been invoked when the headphones were plugged in was not. Called support. They told me to unplug/replug the headphones and the sound configuration panel would appear. It didn't. Told me to plug the headphones in the socket at the back of the PC. Inconvenient but the sound was working from the rear socket. Told me to use that instead. When I said this was not acceptable I was told to take the side off the PC and check that the plug was seated correctly in the motherboard. I'm 60 years old; I paid for someone else to build a system for me precisely because I don't want to have to be grubbing around on the floor taking PCs apart. Nonetheless, I agreed and was told that he (the support guy) would be waiting for my call back. Eventually I got the side off and found the plug was seated fine. However, I could not get back through to support - no-one answered the phone. Admittedly it was 16:45 on a Friday afternoon but nonetheless if someone says to me they'll wait for a call (and he did only have to wait 10 minutes) I expect them to do just that. The final outcome? There were two plugs on the wire that connected to the motherboard, one marked AC97 (which was plugged in) and the other, tied back was marked HD. Reasoning that it wasn't working anyway and it probably wouldn't do any harm, I swapped the plugs around - and found that the front headphone socket then worked. Problem solved ... but not by DinoPC. Reading various articles on the internet after this farrago revealed that this is quite a common problem and that whichever plug is used the BIOS must be set appropriately. Evidently my PC was not properly configured and therefore could not have been fully tested before it left DinoPC. I emphasize the 'fully'. So, a minor fault in the build, quality control less than par, and not a great experience with support. Would I use them again? No I wouldn't, which in a way is a pity because the system itself is pretty good, however, when I am paying almost £800 for a PC I expect it to work out-of-the-box and if I doesn't I expect exemplary support. My opionion is that if DinoPC really cares about its customers (and I have no reason really to suppose that they don't) and want to do well then they need to (a) tighten up their quality control and (b) improve their after-sales support.

The cars are late model cars with very few kilometers on the odometer and have unlimited kilometers. I rented a Toyota hybrid and I got an average use of 4.3 liter/100 kilometer. Also the rental allows travel in other countries other than the country in which you rent the car. There are some restriction so please check the on-line information. Parking is a problem in Europe, however, my comments are specifically directed at parking in the Netherlands. First, there are several "blue zones" for short-term parking. You will be ticketed if you do not have a blue disc that is used to indicated when you arrived. The parking is free for the allowed duration, but without the blue disc you can be toast. Blue discs can be purchased at any bookstore for about 1.80 Euro. Next, everything is done with chip cards; that is something that we don't use in the US and many parking automates do not take anything but credit and debit cards with chips on them (chipcards). Some do still take coins, but not very many do,  so carry single Euros. Other than that you will have to use parking garages or find some free parking, but be careful and make sure it is truly free; I have been ticketed a number of times in the past. Although this extra info did not pertain to the performance of Auto Europe, I felt it important to mention it. As far as the service that Auto Europe provides, it is very, very good and the cost is one of the best in the business. I can highly recommend Auto Europe and you will not be sorry to try them. Trionic goes well-beyond Cobblestones!: In June 2009 my wife and I took my old four-wheeled rollator when we flew to Dresden Germany from Silver Spring, MD USA to visit our son.  He took us on some sight seeing day trips in Dresden, one to Poland and another to Prague in the Czech Republic.  The four-wheeler was very difficult to handle wherever there were cobblestones and curbs without ramps and uneven pavement, which was just about everywhere.  Everyone who has tried will have experienced the abrupt halting of movement when a wide crack or bump is in the way. . . or the locking up of wheels between stones . . . or the necessity to lift the walker up steps and over obstructions Following that trip I knew that there had to be a better walker.  On another trip on a ferry boat the four-wheeler did its little front-wheel-spin-dance, that some have dubbed the shopping cart syndrome, on an apparently "flat," but actually uneven surface.  Once again, this was a common experience for four-wheeled rollator users. Then, I searched the internet for a "three-wheeled rollator with seat."  I needed the seat for an occasional sit-down to alleviate pain from my spinal stenosis. Voila! Google located for me the Trionic All Terrain Walker.  I waisted more than a year in the hopes of seeing one of these Velopeds in action to determine whether I really wanted to purchase one.  None were to be found near my part of the USA. In November 2010, my wife and I took a Nile Riverboat trip to many ancient sites in Egypt using my four-wheeled rollator.  What a mistake that I had not yet purchased the Trionic All-Terrain! Talk about cobblestone and uneven surfaces in the temples of Luxor or gravel surfaces in the Valley of the Kings!  Or worse still, the walking surfaces to and around the Temples at Abu Simbel!  That Egypt trip would have been the perfect place to try out what the literatures said the Trionic would do.  I would love to go again on the same trip with my new Trionic.  What a TEST that would be!  In fact, I would like to take the trip again with a professional video crew just to demonstrate how the Trionic would function in such circumstances.  That would make very convincing footage to be placed on YouTube. After the Nile River trip I returned to the USA fully convinced that I had to have a Trionic walker before I ever again went anywhere where there might be so many impediments to my mobility.  I looked at the internet adds again, pouring over the various online videos, and called two suppliers, still looking to see a demonstration of a Trionic.  No luck! Finally, in January 2011 I saw what may have been a "once-in-a-lifetime" add showing a used demo Trionic.   I immediately bought my Trionic Veloped "as is" as a pre-used Demonstration model from ElderLuxe, a supplier located in Chicago, Illinois, USA.  It was being sold for $150 below list price, so I didn't have choices of stripe colors or any other features.  I wondered what might have been wrong with it for such a good price. When the large box containing my Trionic arrived I was pleasantly surprised.  No damage or apparent scars or anything terrible. The pressure on one  tire was a little low.  Easily fixed!  The braking lever on the left side was weak, but that too was easily adjusted. I used the Trionic in our retirement community a couple of times to discover that it worked just fine inside and outside.  It accomplished all that it was said to do even climbing a 5" (12.7 cm) curb.  It's footprint was a bit larger than the four-wheeler so there was a tighter fit in the elevators.  It drew the attention of several residents, but was accepted when I explained why there was that funny looking "free spinning" extra wheel in front. On several occasions I used my Trionic for taking walks on gravel and sandy surfaces in Fenwick Island, Delaware, USA.  It worked beautifully to my satisfaction.  These were walks I simply would not have attempted with my cane or my four-wheeled rollator.   Getting to Delaware and home again was no problem at all.   The Trionic folded into a very compact bundle to go into the trunk of our car.  I'm not sure it was absolutely necessary, but I removed the wheels with the easy-to-operate quick-release features.  It was so well designed.  Very well engineered. Most recently, my wife and I went on a planned cruise to the Hawiian Islands.  It was necessary for us to fly on an airline from Washington, DC to Los Angeles, CA before boarding our cruise ship, the Sapphire Princess.  Though we had some mental reservations, I was determined to take my Trionic Rollator to see how well it traveled.  I wasn't sure how airport shuttle services would deal with it, nor the airport security checkpoints, nor the airline, nor the cruise ship, nor the various shore excursion buses that we used  at each of the four islands that we visited.  Without going into great detail, I can only say that my Trionic passed aal of these tests in every way.  And I was very favorably impressed about how my mobility was increased in so many ways in so many places. In airports and on the cruise ships other passengers often looked at my walker and  did a double-take,  looking at it again.  I guess they were trying to figure out why my walker had such big tires or why on earth I had a "spare tire" spinning around next to my front  wheel.  On board ship, several people commented, "I have never seen one like that!"  Others said, "That looks like the Cadillac of walkers!"  Several people inquired about the Trionic, and I explained it as an "All-Terrain" rollator which went over obstacles and was especially good for exterior use on uneven and rough surfaces such all the cobblestone found in Europe. On two or three occasions I even demonstrated how the Trionic folded laterally and even removed the wheels to show how it could become very compact when required.  Cruise ship cabin doors are narrow as are the walkways (especially when laundry carts or suitcases are parked in them).  The Trionic lateral movement folding motion solved those problems easily.  Trionic worked for me in every test circumstance I gave it. But one of the real thrills for me was when I could walk in loose lava gravel over some rough rocks (about three or four inches high) at the observation area on the extinct volcano Kileakawa on the Island of Maui, Hawaii USA.  We were almost 10,000 feet high.  The wind was blowing briskly.  There were billowing clouds coming below us on the eastern (windward) side of the Island.  The vista was beautiful.  That vista is something I would have missed completely had it been necessary for me to rely on an old four-wheeled walker or the use of my walking cane. Since returning home I have decided to use my computer to print a brief description from the sales literature about the Trionic walker, make lots of copies, and hand one to each person in the future who may want information about this fabulous device.  I feel sort of like a traveling representative for Trionic.  I am happy to share my satisfaction with others who may want to remain more active even though they have some some physical infirmity.  I will include the company website on my "sales" handouts so others can pursue further information. I hope to continue using my Trionic for as long as I am able to walk with the assistance of an all-terrain walker. Look out!  Here we come!
